title: Evaluating Compressed Memory: Dependence, Utility, and Content Benefit
abstract: arXiv:2610.19373v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Does a language model answer better because its compressed memory contains useful document information? Replacing memory vectors with zeros can lower a trained model's score without showing that it outperforms a model trained without memory. We combine zeroing with separately trained models that cannot access stored text or receive the same constant input for every document. Across nine systems, some models rely on memory yet perform worse than the trained alternative. For example, in experiments that predict states in generated stories, zeroing memory worsens a model's prediction loss, yet a model trained without memory achieves lower loss than the original model with intact memory. On TriviaQA, giving xRAG memory from another question's passage raises F1, which measures word overlap with accepted answers, from 19.38 without a document to 24.78. translated_title: 评估压缩记忆：依赖性、效用与内容收益
translated_abstract: 语言模型的回答更好，是因为其压缩记忆中包含了有用的文档信息吗？将记忆向量替换为零可以降低已训练模型的分数，但这并不能证明它优于一个在没有记忆的情况下训练的模型。我们将置零方法与单独训练的对照模型相结合——这些对照模型无法访问存储的文本，或对每个文档都接收相同的常量输入。在九个系统中，一些模型虽然依赖记忆，但其表现却不如训练过的替代方案。例如，在预测生成故事中状态的实验里，将记忆置零会恶化模型的预测损失，然而在没有记忆情况下训练的模型却比拥有完整记忆的原始模型取得了更低的损失。在TriviaQA上，为xRAG提供来自另一个问题段落的记忆，将衡量输出与标准答案词重合度的F1分数从无文档时的19.38提高到24.78，但其对输出包含标准答案频率的影响在统计上并不确定。
tldr: 该论文提出将记忆置零与无法访问存储文本的对照模型相结合来严格评估压缩记忆的真实效用，发现某些依赖记忆的模型性能反而不如无记忆训练的替代模型。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes rigorously evaluating compressed memory utility by combining memory zeroing with control models that cannot access stored text, finding that some memory-dependent models perform worse than alternatives trained without memory.
